title: Force Multiplier:100 simulated MXMGR perspectives
method: 100 AI-constructed evaluation perspectives,20 per specialty, spanning five experience groups and four world/play contexts. Not real participants, votes, learner outcomes or measured usability. Verified software findings are distinguished from predicted reactions.

personas.value: A newcomer can begin by selecting aircraft without reading a maintenance manual.
personas.concern: The first request for a hint earns fewer stars than repeated failed checks, which may discourage asking how the game works.

personas.value: The Bus Company setting makes the relationship between vehicles and repeated trips approachable.
personas.concern: Later boards could feel like a large amount of scrolling and repeated tapping on a phone; confirm this with actual phone users.

personas.value: Named buttons and aircraft labels support keyboard access to the opening exercises.
personas.concern: Primary actions could lose keyboard focus after rerendering in the baseline build.

personas.value: The level map lets a curious newcomer see the destination before committing to a sequence.
personas.concern: Skipping directly to a checkerboard may bypass the cues that explain curing and work placement.

personas.value: The shared-cure exercise makes a scheduling efficiency visible as fewer grounded days.
personas.concern: A learner should be able to explain why the shared cure is valid in this fictional model before transferring the shortcut to real work.

personas.value: Small daily missions give a practical foothold before the whole checkerboard appears.
personas.concern: The jump from9 core actions in level6 to48 in level7 may add input effort faster than it adds new concepts.

personas.value: Undo and source-specific error messages make incorrect assignments recoverable.
personas.concern: A later112-cell board remains cumbersome to traverse one Tab at a time even after focus is repaired.

personas.value: The final outage provides a reason to revise an existing plan rather than rebuild mindlessly.
personas.concern: New cases retain the same structural pattern, so a changed tail number is a limited test of adaptation.

personas.value: Feasible alternatives are accepted; the game does not demand the authors one exact schedule.
personas.concern: The model lacks dock capacity, labor qualifications and other resource constraints needed for a later job-level assessment.

personas.value: A compact checkerboard can make availability and commitments visible together.
personas.concern: The135 core actions in level12 may reward patience with tapping as well as planning skill.

personas.value: Cell labels identify aircraft, day and wave status rather than relying on color alone.
personas.concern: A keyboard scheduler needs predictable continuation at the next relevant work cell after each command.

personas.value: Direct level access respects an experienced scheduler who already understands six-turn-four.
personas.concern: Every generated capstone is solvable; there is no decision about escalating impossible demand or accepting a tradeoff.

personas.value: The progression isolates useful teaching points, especially active work versus elapsed curing.
personas.concern: The trainer cannot yet ask the game to distinguish guided practice from a separate unseen independent assessment.

personas.value: Students can enter the game on a browser without a large document download.
personas.concern: Students on multiple devices will not automatically bring their progress or artifacts to a shared trainer view.

personas.value: Worked examples are marked as demonstrations and do not earn independent stars.
personas.concern: Zero demo stars are useful, but completion alone does not show whether the learner could reproduce the reasoning.

personas.value: A trainer can move directly to a selected challenge during a discussion.
personas.concern: The working group needs an easy way to inspect the finished work and the reason for choices, beyond the star total.

personas.value: The final model checks both maintenance work and flying commitments.
personas.concern: A two-week eight-asset solution does not yet demonstrate the users larger occupational capstone.

personas.value: Airline and Bus Company make the underlying resource-allocation problem recognizable outside military vocabulary.
personas.concern: A whimsical world may engage some staff and distract others; preference needs real-user observation, not an invented approval percentage.

personas.value: Explicitly bounded game rules help separate fictional practice from actual maintenance instructions.
personas.concern: A supervisor should interpret stars as game feedback, not as evidence of independent job qualification.

personas.value: The changed-demand level is a useful starting point for a scenario-based working-group discussion.
personas.concern: The app still needs a final communicate-and-defend activity to match the full performance framework.

personas.value: Selecting completed jobs introduces the distinction between planned and finished work through an action.
personas.concern: The completed-job target count is visible, so this proves classification more directly than independent counting.

personas.value: The first analysis cases are short enough to enter without facing a spreadsheet full of numbers.
personas.concern: A newcomer may avoid Hint because of the scoring penalty even when the instruction is unfamiliar.

personas.value: Number tiles and source records are ordinary buttons with labels.
personas.concern: The baseline primary Check action needed stable focus after feedback.

personas.value: A newcomer can try a chart challenge directly and return to counting when ready.
personas.concern: Jumping to pooled reports without learning denominator scope may create guessing rather than a useful challenge.

personas.value: Assembling the numerator and denominator makes the rate structure visible.
personas.concern: Both pooled/report denominators were always100 in the baseline. This memorization shortcut is now corrected for new cases.

personas.value: Moving tokens to balance four stacks gives a concrete image of the mean.
personas.concern: Only whole-number means from four stacks are practiced, so fractional averages need a later bridge.

personas.value: The missing-value case requires the matching day and unit, not only the right number.
personas.concern: A correct filled value must remain tied to its evidence after later edits; the reducer tests verify this behavior.

personas.value: The first report requires selecting the correct time window instead of including every visible row.
personas.concern: Fixed answer sets can demonstrate recognition without requiring the learner to construct an explanation.

personas.value: Pooling actual counts teaches why group size matters.
personas.concern: Unequal groups need varied totals; baseline totals of100 did not adequately vary the denominator. New cases now do.

personas.value: Comparing equal means with different spreads introduces a useful operational distinction.
personas.concern: The spread lesson uses range alone; a later extension should distinguish range, distribution and sample size.

personas.value: Charts include text descriptions and visible observation values.
personas.concern: Level was an impossible correct answer in baseline trend/scatter replay. Neutral cases are now included.

personas.value: The game rewards a scoped statement rather than a claim guaranteed forever.
personas.concern: The final report does not yet combine trends, variation or unfamiliar evidence into the same decision.

personas.value: The stages separate counting, rates, center, missing data, trends and reporting.
personas.concern: The introductory sequence is promising, but a trainer still needs an unseen transfer task before claiming learning.

personas.value: The simple game can be an approachable first exposure before a larger statistics lab.
personas.concern: Repeated fixed-layout scenarios may teach where to click; vary the problem structure after the basics.

personas.value: Reducers preserve prior states, and Undo supports discussing a mistaken analytical step.
personas.concern: Keyboard focus and concise error feedback matter when a trainer demonstrates a wrong denominator live.

personas.value: A trainer can select the exact concept that a learner is having trouble applying.
personas.concern: The neutral scatter correction must say no clear linear trend rather than claiming that no relationship exists; the patch does.

personas.value: A correct rate requires the right records and matching counts, not merely a plausible percentage.
personas.concern: Completion stars do not show that a learner can investigate a bad source, make a decision and defend it independently.

personas.value: World vocabulary connects the same analytic structure to flights, runs, visits or missions.
personas.concern: Changing the world alone does not add a distinct industry data model or demonstrate occupational transfer.

personas.value: The code explicitly rejects causal conclusions drawn only from the shown scatter.
personas.concern: No causal choice is valid in these observational scenarios, appropriately; later learning should still demand reasoning beyond remembering that rule.

personas.value: The last challenge assembles a small report from competing records and a time window.
personas.concern: A supervisor needs inspectable evidence of the actual report and rationale, not only a best score.

personas.value: The first record match gives an immediate, concrete starting point.
personas.concern: A newcomer may mistake the act of attaching a requirement for evidence that the inspection itself is complete.

personas.value: Short prompts and large asset cards offer a manageable first phone task.
personas.concern: Small applicability and interval metadata may require zooming on a physical phone.

personas.value: Buttons and explicit labels can support keyboard-only play.
personas.concern: The baseline capstone reused answer-focus identities and could silently focus the next correct answer.

personas.value: Open level selection lets an impatient learner explore the later work pack.
personas.concern: Skipping to the final pack can produce a completion badge without practicing applicability or forecast decisions.

personas.value: Combining family and serial range is more useful than memorizing a definition.
personas.concern: Exact target counts may let a learner stop searching when the meter fills rather than verifying applicability.

personas.value: The first-due-day challenge clearly introduces two competing limits.
personas.concern: The fixed-use forecast may look easier than a changing operational forecast, and compact source cards need a real-phone check.

personas.value: The register supports alternative valid row ordering.
personas.concern: A replacement records only a short Linked message, so the old interval is not visible in the register trail.

personas.value: New cases change asset numbers and intervals.
personas.concern: The final five-choice structure remains predictable even when numbers change.

personas.value: Current, draft and superseded copies teach a useful source-control distinction.
personas.concern: A veteran may find a single Approved choice too obvious to exercise judgment.

personas.value: The matching-work-plus-passed-check closeout is a practical distinction.
personas.concern: The strongest evidence labels become small on phone layouts; real users should confirm they can compare them easily.

personas.value: Either parts-first or slot-first is accepted when prerequisites are satisfied.
personas.concern: The baseline auto-advance focus rewarded repeated activation instead of deliberate inspection of the next stage.

personas.value: The work-pack path brings several basic decisions together quickly.
personas.concern: It still cues each target and has no conflicting sources, changed demand or reasoned defense.

personas.value: A trainer can demonstrate wrong applicability, wrong revisions and invalid closeouts safely.
personas.concern: Stars alone do not show which concept the learner misunderstood or whether the learner can repeat the task independently.

personas.value: A trainer can use the phone-friendly cards during short practice sessions.
personas.concern: Hint scoring could discourage a learner from requesting the help the trainer wants them to use.

personas.value: Keyboard play can make a projector walkthrough efficient.
personas.concern: Automatic focus must move to the next stage, not a preselected correct answer; the pack fix now supplies that target.

personas.value: Direct access to any level helps a trainer target a weak skill.
personas.concern: A later unseen work-product challenge is needed if the trainer wants evidence beyond recognition of the displayed cues.

personas.value: The model accepts valid alternatives and enforces prerequisite logic.
personas.concern: A supervisor should not read a best-star total as demonstrated job qualification.

personas.value: Short sessions can fit around work without a long lesson page.
personas.concern: The supervisor still needs observable work products and a practical review rubric to compare learners.

personas.value: The correct-current-source rule and reopened closeout reinforce documentation discipline.
personas.concern: The simpler register history should eventually preserve before/after detail so both record specialties teach compatible audit habits.

personas.value: World changes show that the underlying record skills are broader than one aircraft community.
personas.concern: Changing the label to a bus or rover does not by itself establish transfer to a different occupation.

personas.value: One wrong number gives a novice an easy first success.
personas.concern: The Match source button performs the correction automatically; a novice can succeed without identifying the mismatched field.

personas.value: Unknown and zero appear side by side with short labels.
personas.concern: Their small metadata should remain readable on a real phone so the distinction is not reduced to blind tapping.

personas.value: Source and record cards make the evidence relationship visible.
personas.concern: An already-correct retained row originally had no persistent reviewed marker after keyboard verification.

personas.value: Immediate corrections make experimentation feel safe.
personas.concern: An impatient player may press Match source on every row and learn the button sequence more readily than the verification habit.

personas.value: Unit conversion requires choosing both a number and a unit.
personas.concern: A later mixed-unit batch would be needed to see whether this carries over when the unit mismatch is not announced in the prompt.

personas.value: Event IDs and times make duplicate comparison concrete.
personas.concern: Side-by-side comparisons and small labels may become tiring on a phone during a larger batch.

personas.value: Linking child records to existing parents gives a concrete identity task.
personas.concern: The reviewed-state marker was necessary so keyboard users could keep their place in a mixed batch.

personas.value: Keeping zero-result records teaches a useful reconciliation habit.
personas.concern: The exact expected record count is displayed, so the task does not yet assess when the search is complete.

personas.value: Duplicate events are distinguished from similar but separate events.
personas.concern: An experienced reviewer will want ambiguous duplicates and investigation choices, beyond identical event copies.

personas.value: The current-source challenge correctly rejects a newer draft.
personas.concern: There is always exactly one Approved choice; real source disputes require more than noticing that label.

personas.value: The before-and-after audit trail is a useful foundation.
personas.concern: Baseline review of an unchanged record was invisible, making a correct batch harder to inspect; that display issue is now fixed.

personas.value: The prevention gate holds errors while retaining valid zeros.
personas.concern: The final batch still supplies the authoritative answer beside every row and copies whole records in one action.

personas.value: A trainer can demonstrate why an unknown cannot be changed to zero.
personas.concern: The trainer needs a later task that requires the learner to choose a correction, not merely request an automatic copy.

personas.value: Short tasks can support frequent practice and immediate discussion.
personas.concern: The star cost of hints may undermine the trainer’s invitation to ask for help.

personas.value: Persistent Reviewed indicators now make it easier to explain which rows have been checked.
personas.concern: Keyboard and screen-reader behavior still needs live-user validation rather than relying solely on render tests.

personas.value: A trainer can jump to the exact misconception: units, duplicates, period or source.
personas.concern: Completing a targeted example does not show independent transfer to an unfamiliar combined case.

personas.value: The gate checks model prevention as well as cleanup.
personas.concern: A supervisor would need evidence that learners can distinguish hold/investigate from correct when sources conflict.

personas.value: Local browser play makes a small exercise easy to start.
personas.concern: Current stars do not offer a comparable assessor portfolio or explanation of judgment.

personas.value: Audit validation checks more than whether the final number happens to be right.
personas.concern: Record review and correction history should become part of a larger work-product assessment, not be inferred from stars.

personas.value: Airline, bus, cat and squirrel contexts make the same record relationships approachable.
personas.concern: The contexts share the same underlying task patterns; they are not evidence of four independent occupational validations.

personas.value: One request and three keys make the first action easy to understand.
personas.concern: I may assume Edit alone is enough until I notice that viewing and editing are separate capabilities in this game.

personas.value: A short instruction and a few buttons suit a quick practice break.
personas.concern: I need the task, person, scope and selected keys to remain visible together on a small display; this requires browser observation, not a claim from code alone.

personas.value: Labeled buttons and stable focus identifiers give a basis for keyboard interaction.
personas.concern: I want a real keyboard walkthrough to confirm that a repaired/re-rendered board does not strand focus; this review did not use a browser.

personas.value: I can jump to the task that catches my attention and return to fundamentals.
personas.concern: If I skip straight to the final service challenge, I may click failure markers without understanding the approval and change sequence.

personas.value: Permissions, room scope and temporary passes connect to everyday account work.
personas.concern: The old identity labels let me choose Approved without reading the unique ID; neutral labels now make that distinction meaningful.

personas.value: Local saved work lets me leave a short task and return to it on the same browser.
personas.concern: My progress will not automatically follow from my phone to a work computer, and an evaluator cannot infer that these are the same learner.

personas.value: Wrong ordering is rejected and I can correct a sequence instead of starting a long lesson again.
personas.concern: The detailed error tells me the right order; the resulting corrected-work stars should not be treated as an independent assessment.

personas.value: The final challenge combines access, a dependency and a safe change in one place.
personas.concern: Repeated final cases previously reused the same action pattern; varied tasks and failures now require me to read the case again.

personas.value: The early levels are a useful quick check of least-privilege and access-lifecycle habits.
personas.concern: A directly marked failed node is too simple to establish that I can diagnose an interface fault from ambiguous symptoms.

personas.value: The modular path lets me practice during short intervals without a setup procedure.
personas.concern: I would need a later recovery task that validates actual records; matching a count alone leaves important integrity questions unasked.

personas.value: The duplicate-name exercise rewards a precise identifier comparison after the label shortcut was removed.
personas.concern: The case still tests a small predetermined permission set; my broader judgement about approvals and exceptional access is not measured.

personas.value: Level selection lets me bypass already-familiar introductory key puzzles.
personas.concern: Four different worlds are context changes around the same mechanics, so completing each is not four independent occupational qualifications.

personas.value: Working examples and repeatable seeded cases support demonstration followed by guided practice.
personas.concern: A zero-star demo used to display the same completed checkmark as independent work; the distinction must survive menus and progress summaries.

personas.value: One concept per short task offers a practical way to observe a learner without a slide presentation.
personas.concern: I need to see whether the learner avoids Hint to protect stars; that effect cannot be established by this simulated panel.

personas.value: Separate world and specialty progress supports individual pacing and returning to unfinished work.
personas.concern: A trainer still needs a way to record the reason behind a learner decision and compare independent performance across unfamiliar cases.

personas.value: The now-varied final DBM case is more useful for asking a learner to inspect each new request.
personas.concern: The same visible failure cues and fixed safe-change sequence still make this practice, not a fully independent practical examination.

personas.value: The five-specialty structure makes the expected fundamentals visible and easy to discuss with a working group.
personas.concern: I cannot answer who is ready to perform the full job from game completion alone; I need an unfamiliar work product and its defense.

personas.value: A browser game lowers the effort required to demonstrate the concept to colleagues.
personas.concern: Local browser scores are not an auditable team proficiency record and may be lost when moving devices or clearing data.

personas.value: The playful setting can make the same permission and record concepts approachable outside aviation.
personas.concern: Accessibility and appeal still need observation with actual users; this role simulation is not evidence of adoption or training effectiveness.

personas.value: Open navigation makes it easy to inspect later tasks without completing every earlier screen.
personas.concern: Fast completion, including using examples, must not be used to claim the four-hour or tenfold training targets were achieved.

findings.observation: Scheduling introduces counts, priority, unavailability, person-specific assignments, work occupancy, curing, compatible work, weekends, mixed commitments and replanning in successive levels. Core validators accept alternative feasible aircraft selections and work placements.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified source and model behavior
findings.reproduction: Ran node tests/game-rules.cjs: 13 levels, 1,300 seeded models, 32,052 assertions. Includes alternative work placements and reverse aircraft selections.
findings.recommendation: Preserve constraint-based validation and the short initial interaction.

findings.observation: The Analysis path teaches by classifying jobs, assembling rates, moving conserved tokens, sorting observations, linking missing values to evidence and manipulating chart choices. Inputs and examples pass through immutable reducers.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified source and reducer tests
findings.reproduction: Baseline suite passed 4,996 assertions across 12 levels × 20 seeds with actual reducer paths, invalid-work checks and provenance validation.
findings.recommendation: Keep direct actions and short post-success explanations; use these as the entry point.

findings.observation: Baseline Analysis levels 5 and 12 always used a pooled denominator of 100. A player could memorize that denominator and avoid transferring the pooling operation to different group totals.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified generator restriction; learning consequence is a hypothesis
findings.reproduction: Generated 100 seeds per level before editing: unique eligible totals were [100] for both levels.
findings.recommendation: Vary unequal group sizes and totals while preserving integer counts. Implemented in revision 2; revision 1 retains saved cases.

findings.observation: Baseline trend and scatter levels displayed a Level response but only generated up/down answers. Repeated play could learn that the neutral response was never valid.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified generator restriction; guessing behavior is a hypothesis
findings.reproduction: Generated 100 baseline seeds per level: directions were only up/down.
findings.recommendation: Implemented level time series and scattered weak-linear-pattern cases. Neutral scatter uses a bounded No linear trend claim and does not claim independence.

findings.observation: Scheduling level 12 requires 110 individual flight selections, 20 wave confirmations, four work placements and the Plan flights transition: at least135 core actions from a blank board. Level 6 needs 9 core actions and level 7 needs 48. Mechanical repetition may begin to dominate later practice.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: action counts verified from generated scenario; fatigue is a usability hypothesis
findings.reproduction: Counted required assignments, confirmations, work placements and transition from seeded scenarios; excludes navigation, retries and extra selections.
findings.recommendation: After a learner demonstrates a day manually, consider a copy-day action that still exposes and validates changed constraints. Validate with observed real learners before adding automation.

findings.observation: The current Scheduling finish checks an executable two-week model, but does not require a learner to explain a tradeoff, communicate a handover, defend the plan, or solve an infeasible demand case. Analysis level 12 checks report scope and pooled rate, not the entire statistical path.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified scope of automated checks; effectiveness cannot be inferred
findings.reproduction: Inspected final-level generators, checkers, finish and saved-state fields. No required rationale, peer review, or communication work product is present in the game paths.
findings.recommendation: Use the game as fundamentals practice. Add a later unfamiliar combined mission with a small decision artifact and human review before treating stars as job-proficiency evidence.

findings.observation: A single Hint lowers the maximum score for the current case to one star, while any number of failed checks can still earn two. This makes a deliberate request for instruction look worse than repeated unassisted guessing.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: scoring rule verified; learner avoidance is a hypothesis
findings.reproduction: Read finish() precedence and showHelp(); hints are recorded before the dialog opens.
findings.recommendation: Consider separating practice help from a later independent challenge, or showing coached/independent badges without presenting help-seeking as poorer learning.

findings.observation: Baseline Check, Plan flights and Set wave controls lacked stable focus identifiers although render() replaced the entire UI. Keyboard focus could be lost after checking or changing a board wave. A large board also places many cells in the normal tab sequence.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: missing focus identifiers verified from source; root handles browser confirmation
findings.reproduction: Compare action controls against render() focus-restoration logic. Pack tiles and aircraft cells already had data-focus; primary check controls did not.
findings.recommendation: Root is adding stable focus restoration. Separately consider arrow-key grid navigation for the checkerboard.
findings.status: Fixed for primary check/action controls. Browser verification passed. Arrow-key grid navigation remains a recommendation.

findings.observation: Mean uses exactly four integer-balance stacks; median uses five distinct values; scatter/report claims use a small fixed option set. These make a clear introduction but do not yet exercise even-sized medians, fractional means, sample-size uncertainty or a learner-authored explanation.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified content scope; transfer difficulty is a hypothesis
findings.reproduction: Inspected scenario families and final checks. No even-sized median or inferential statistics case is generated in the new game path.
findings.recommendation: Extend later levels only after validating these foundations; keep the initial game uncluttered.

findings.observation: All four worlds reuse the same underlying models with different vocabulary, vehicles and progress tracks. Different-world success alone would not establish transfer to independent industry constraints.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified implementation scope; transfer measurement is a design inference
findings.reproduction: The same Flight engine and Analysis pack are used for every world; world values are passed to rendering.
findings.recommendation: Retain playful worlds. Later use genuinely different constraint sets and unseen tasks when testing transfer, rather than counting a skin change as a new occupational test.

findings.observation: Stars and current work are browser-local. The main game does not provide a trainer report/export of decisions, mistakes or work products, unlike the separate earlier practice workspace.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified main-game feature scope
findings.reproduction: Inspected persistence shape and menu actions; localStorage contains current state and best stars but no trainer-facing export action.
findings.recommendation: A working-group pilot needs a lightweight results sheet or separate observation form; add an optional work-product export later without interrupting play.

findings.observation: Baseline Documentation level 10 reused the same answer focus keys across auto-advanced tabs. After choosing the correct first asset, focus could land on the correct answer in every following tab, allowing repeated Enter to supply the remaining answers.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified source/model defect; browser reproduction is owned by root.
findings.reproduction: For seeds 1–20, every tab contained data-focus="doc-pack-a" and id a was the correct choice; repeating that focus identity solved all five links. Baseline probe: records-probes.cjs.
findings.recommendation: Give options slot-specific focus keys and move focus to the next tab control after choosing an answer.
findings.status: Fixed in pack and shared shell. Browser verified focus moves to the next stage tab, not its correct answer.

findings.observation: Baseline Integrity level 10 recorded review of an already-correct row internally but rendered an identical board before and after; the player had no persistent per-row sign that review was complete.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified source/render defect.
findings.reproduction: Copy/verify row d in level 10 for seeds1–20. reviewed gains d but the complete rendered board HTML was identical.
findings.recommendation: Persist a Reviewed label/checkmark and accessible pressed state for reviewed rows.
findings.status: Fixed. Browser verified visible/accessibility Reviewed state; model probes cover already-correct rows.

findings.observation: Integrity levels 1,2,8 and10 correct every field via one Match source action. The final batch still supplies the authoritative source beside each record and one-click correction; it does not require selecting which fields or source facts support a correction.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified interaction scope; possible effect on independent proficiency is a hypothesis.
findings.reproduction: The copy reducer replaces the whole record with sources[eventId], including identity,value and units.
findings.recommendation: Keep this as initial scaffolding; add a later challenge with plausible source candidates, field-level corrections and a choice of keep, correct, hold, or investigate.
findings.status: Backlog; not changed during focused fixes.

findings.observation: The Documentation final pack is five cued choices. Its source card tells the required asset, approved revision, kit and acceptable timing; it does not make the player discover requirements from an unfamiliar work product or defend a decision.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified curriculum scope; transfer concern is a hypothesis.
findings.reproduction: Follow the five labeled tabs; each shows three candidates and explicit target details.
findings.recommendation: Follow the game foundation with a short unfamiliar case that combines applicability, due forecasting, register reconciliation and closeout evidence without identifying every target first.

findings.observation: Documentation forecasting uses exact constant daily usage and integer days. It teaches the earlier-of-two-limits rule, but not changed demand, fractional threshold crossing or forecasting uncertainty.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified model simplification; difficulty or real-world transfer effect needs users.
findings.reproduction: Level 5 sets limit=now+daily*usageDays and compares that exact day with a calendar day.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the simple first exercise and add a later changed-use-rate case or one that asks whether more evidence is needed.

findings.observation: Documentation register repair stores trail strings such as Linked R-123 or Archived R-OLD; replacing a row does not retain its old interval or old row contents in that trail. Integrity later teaches a fuller before-and-after trail.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified difference in modeled traceability; instructional inconsistency risk is a hypothesis.
findings.reproduction: Replace the incorrect interval in Documentation9; p.trail records the linked requirement ID but not the previous interval.
findings.recommendation: In an advanced register exercise, retain before/after/source/reason for replacements and archive actions, consistent with Integrity.

findings.observation: A hint limits a case to one star, while failed checks followed by correction can still earn two. The game therefore rewards unsupported trial-and-error more highly than intentionally asking for help.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified scoring rule; whether it discourages help is a simulated-user hypothesis.
findings.reproduction: finish chooses assisted?0:hints?1:mistakes?2:3.
findings.recommendation: Keep assisted and independent attempts distinguishable, but consider separate practice rewards and independent-check badges so learners are not discouraged from opening a hint.
findings.status: Backlog; no change to established scoring during this review.

findings.observation: Worlds change context labels, icons, vehicles and seed/progress state; the core Documentation and Integrity task structures stay the same.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified architecture; user preferences and transfer to civilian occupations remain hypotheses.
findings.reproduction: Render any case with each world object; requirements and validators remain the same.
findings.recommendation: Describe these as contextual worlds around shared fundamentals. Later add genuinely different constraints when industry-specific transfer is the goal.

findings.observation: The game shell primarily preserves current work and best stars. It does not present an assessor with a comparable portfolio showing reasoning, unseen-case performance and an explanation rubric across the two record specialties.
source: README.md: game scope versus preserved courses workspace
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified current game scope; sufficiency for job qualification must be evaluated separately.
findings.reproduction: Game completion shows stars and a short reveal, then next-level/new-case/review choices.
findings.recommendation: Keep stars as game feedback. Add an optional later independent work-product challenge and assessor rubric if the working group wants evidence of practical proficiency.
findings.status: Backlog; not a claim of measured training effectiveness.

findings.observation: Several compact-screen metadata labels are rendered at 9–10px; record comparison and register tasks rely on these details.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: CSS sizes verified; readability concern is a hypothesis requiring real device/user testing.
findings.reproduction: Inspect sg-card-meta, sg-label and sg-note in the small-screen rules.
findings.recommendation: Check on a physical phone with typical users; prioritize asset IDs, intervals, units and source status over decorative labels, and support enlarged text.

findings.observation: Documentation validators correctly enforce both applicability conditions, current approved instructions, prerequisite order, matching evidence and the absence of duplicate/extra requirements. Alternative register row order and either parts/slot prerequisite order are accepted.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified by source and passing model/event tests.
findings.reproduction: Run tests/pack-documentation.cjs; checks include extra tagged assets, draft revisions, reordered valid prerequisites, duplicate requirements and alternative register order.
findings.recommendation: Retain these checks and acceptance of valid alternatives.

findings.observation: Current-source exercises show one approved source, one superseded source and one draft. They do not yet include two approved versions with different effective dates or conflicting authoritative records.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified scenario pattern; risk of learning only the Approved label is a hypothesis.
findings.reproduction: Generate any seed; source status categories and correct status remain fixed.
findings.recommendation: Add a later source-selection case with more than one approved-looking record, an effective-date boundary or an unresolved conflict requiring investigation.

findings.observation: Applicability and period-selection meters reveal the number of required selections, which is helpful scaffolding but reduces the need to decide whether the search is complete.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified UI behavior; influence on learning is a hypothesis.
findings.reproduction: Untouched tasks show tagged/records selected against the exact number expected.
findings.recommendation: Keep counts in introductory play; remove the answer-count cue in a later independent challenge while retaining an explicit Check action.

findings.observation: Documentation will not close a job with only a plan, a wrong-asset record or a failed check; editing linked evidence reopens the closeout.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified by model tests.
findings.reproduction: Attempt stamp with incomplete evidence, or remove an evidence link after a valid closeout.
findings.recommendation: Retain the distinction between scheduled and verified-completed work.

findings.observation: Integrity preserves unknown-versus-zero, requires matching units, distinguishes a duplicate event from a similar event, retains zero-result records in period totals, rejects overbroad zero filtering and checks correction history.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified by source and model/event tests.
findings.reproduction: Run tests/pack-integrity.cjs; the negative cases cover each distinction and both valid duplicate-removal alternatives.
findings.recommendation: Retain these fundamentals and make them recur in later mixed challenges.

findings.observation: The ten-level path introduces access keys, scope, expiry, offboarding, unique identity, dependencies, controlled change, recovery, then a combined service challenge. Seeded action tests find each level solvable and reject several important invalid states.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified software behavior; learning benefit remains a hypothesis
findings.reproduction: Run node tests/pack-database.cjs. Original suite passed 2053 assertions; after focused fixes the suite passed 4301.
findings.recommendation: Keep the one-action opening and progressively combined work. Do not add a prerequisite lecture.

findings.observation: Before this review, completing a shown example wrote best[level]=0 yet displayed the same completed checkmark and incremented the same specialty completion count as independent work. This did not award stars, but the completion display blurred the distinction.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified in real shell event harness
findings.reproduction: Database level 1 → Show a working example → Open access → Next level. Persisted best={1:0}; level 1 got class="level-dot done" and check icon; Object.keys(best).length=1.
findings.recommendation: Implemented by root: demonstrations remain recorded but have a distinct demo marker and do not contribute to completed-level counts.
findings.status: fixed by root in shared shell; root reports225 shell assertions passing

findings.observation: The published DBM10 generator changed names and button order but repeated the same two access requests, same excess/missing key positions and same broken connection. One hundred seeds produced one substantive constraint pattern.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified generator limitation; fixed in local source
findings.reproduction: Normalize names and key-bank order; compare actors task/scope/required keys, initial grants and broken dependency across seeds1–100. Before:1 pattern. After:51 patterns, with36 connection,34 database and30 report failures.
findings.recommendation: Implemented varied scope/task pairs, actor access correction positions and failed dependencies. Existing saved DBM10 work keeps revision 1; new cases use revision 2.
findings.status: fixed; revision 1 exactly matches published generator for 100 seeds

findings.observation: The unique-identity exercise originally labeled the target account Approved and the other No request, so a player could find the answer without matching the unique identifier on the source request.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified source/render shortcut; fixed in local source
findings.reproduction: Inspect both account task chips in level 6. Published labels disclosed the requested account. New labels both say View reports; approval and unique ID remain on the separate source request.
findings.recommendation: Implemented neutral account task labels. Preserve the duplicate display name and require the identifier to distinguish accounts.

findings.observation: Recovery verifies only an expected record count after restore/replay. The model has no record contents, reconciliation samples, duplicates or last-transaction evidence to inspect.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified model scope; risk of transfer overconfidence is a hypothesis
findings.reproduction: Level 9 state contains restored,replayed,verified,opened,count. Verify succeeds when count equals snapshot+pending and stage flags are true.
findings.recommendation: Keep count verification as the introductory task. Add a later recovery case that compares sample contents or transaction evidence, ideally crossing into Data Integrity.

findings.observation: Troubleshooting displays the single failed component directly and repairs it with one action. This practices recognizing a dependency and leaving healthy components alone, but does not require diagnosis from incomplete symptoms.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified model scope; experienced-user reaction is simulated
findings.reproduction: Every case has one false node, explicitly labeled with its failure and Tap to repair; healthy-node clicks leave state unchanged.
findings.recommendation: Retain the simple opening. Later introduce an inspect step, downstream symptoms, and a choice of corrective action rather than only clicking the displayed failure.

findings.observation: Main-game stars measure no failed checks, corrected work, hint use and example use. The shell does not collect a rationale, briefing, independent assessor rating, time-to-proficiency record or cross-specialty work product. It therefore does not establish the full Discover→Evaluate→Decide→Act→Communicate→Defend objective.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified main-game evidence scope; proposed evaluation design is a recommendation
findings.reproduction: Inspect persisted current state and best stars, then finish a game level. No communication/defense artifact or assessor rubric is produced by the game path. Earlier practice workspace is separate.
findings.recommendation: Use the game as fundamentals practice. Follow with an unfamiliar combined work task, a brief explanation of choices and independent assessor review; compare with baseline and delayed transfer before claiming four-hour proficiency or tenfold efficiency.

findings.observation: Using a hint reduces the same-case result to one star. A learner focused on collecting stars might avoid asking for help, even during initial learning. No actual learner behavior was observed.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: scoring rule verified; behavioral effect explicitly hypothetical
findings.reproduction: Hint → solve correctly gives one star. A new case resets assistance. Restart and Undo retain it.
findings.recommendation: During a real pilot, observe help-seeking and frustration. Consider separate practice encouragement and independent-challenge badges if star pressure discourages learning.

findings.observation: The main game stores its current case and best stars locally by world and specialty, but it does not expose a portable record of learner decisions for a working-group evaluator. Earlier workspace exports do not represent the new game path.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified implementation boundary; workflow impact is simulated
findings.reproduction: Inspect main game menu and progress object: world/skill/current/best exist; no learner-evidence export action or cross-device account workflow exists.
findings.recommendation: For a pilot, use a short observer sheet or later add an optional local progress/evidence export. Do not interpret browser-local stars as an authenticated qualification record.

findings.observation: A failed keyboard check removed the focused button and left focus on the page body.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified in the published browser before editing, then verified repaired in local preview.
findings.reproduction: Press Enter on Check it with incomplete work. Baseline activeElement was BODY; revised activeElement remains the skill-check BUTTON.
findings.recommendation: Stable focus identifiers now cover primary check and action controls.
findings.status: Fixed and browser verified. Large-grid arrow navigation remains a separate improvement.

implemented_fixes: Analysis pooling and report cases now use unequal groups with totals beyond 100. New cases require finding the denominator.
Let a neutral pattern be correct
Trend cases can be level. Scatter cases can support No linear trend without claiming that no relationship exists.
Documentation moves focus to the next stage tab. It no longer focuses the next correct answer automatically.
Failed checks retain focus on the Check control instead of returning the player to the top-level page.
Data Integrity keeps a Reviewed marker even when the original record was already correct.
Viewed demonstrations get their own marker and no longer increase the completed-level count.
The account cards no longer disclose which same-name account is approved. The player must match the unique identifier.
Database Management changes access tasks, scopes, excess/missing keys and failed dependencies across new cases.

component_reviews.title: Scheduling and Analysis: 40 simulated MXMGR perspectives
component_reviews.disclaimer: AI-authored persona review, not a survey or human playtest. No real participants were recruited. Persona reactions are predictions. Only separately identified source inspections and code/model probes were executed.

coverage.design: Five experience groups × four play contexts per specialty; each context is paired with one world. This is deliberate review coverage, not a demographic estimate.

actual_checks.result: Confirmed totals100-only and up/down-only baseline restrictions
PASS:6670assertions, including new varied totals and neutral cases

actual_checks.command: Deep equality against pre-review generator, all12levels×100seeds
actual_checks.result: PASS:1200legacy cases unchanged under revision1 after removing additive revision/expectedClaim fields

implemented_changes: Analysis revision2 varies unequal group totals for pooled/report challenges.
Analysis revision2 generates level time series and weak-linear-pattern scatter cases with a cautious No linear trend claim.
Analysis revision1 remains available so the shell can restore unfinished baseline cases exactly.
Regression tests preserve legacy inputs and prove newly offered neutral answers can actually be correct.

findings.observation: Scheduling introduces counts, priority, unavailability, person-specific assignments, work occupancy, curing, compatible work, weekends, mixed commitments and replanning in successive levels. Core validators accept alternative feasible aircraft selections and work placements.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified source and model behavior
findings.reproduction: Ran node tests/game-rules.cjs: 13 levels, 1,300 seeded models, 32,052 assertions. Includes alternative work placements and reverse aircraft selections.
findings.recommendation: Preserve constraint-based validation and the short initial interaction.

findings.observation: The Analysis path teaches by classifying jobs, assembling rates, moving conserved tokens, sorting observations, linking missing values to evidence and manipulating chart choices. Inputs and examples pass through immutable reducers.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified source and reducer tests
findings.reproduction: Baseline suite passed 4,996 assertions across 12 levels × 20 seeds with actual reducer paths, invalid-work checks and provenance validation.
findings.recommendation: Keep direct actions and short post-success explanations; use these as the entry point.

findings.observation: Baseline Analysis levels 5 and 12 always used a pooled denominator of 100. A player could memorize that denominator and avoid transferring the pooling operation to different group totals.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified generator restriction; learning consequence is a hypothesis
findings.reproduction: Generated 100 seeds per level before editing: unique eligible totals were [100] for both levels.
findings.recommendation: Vary unequal group sizes and totals while preserving integer counts. Implemented in revision2; revision1 retains saved cases.

findings.observation: Baseline trend and scatter levels displayed a Level response but only generated up/down answers. Repeated play could learn that the neutral response was never valid.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified generator restriction; guessing behavior is a hypothesis
findings.reproduction: Generated 100 baseline seeds per level: directions were only up/down.
findings.recommendation: Implemented level time series and scattered weak-linear-pattern cases. Neutral scatter uses a bounded No linear trend claim and does not claim independence.

findings.observation: Scheduling level12 requires 110 individual flight selections, 20 wave confirmations, four work placements and the Plan flights transition: at least135 core actions from a blank board. Level6 needs9 core actions and level7 needs48. Mechanical repetition may begin to dominate later practice.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: action counts verified from generated scenario; fatigue is a usability hypothesis
findings.reproduction: Counted required assignments, confirmations, work placements and transition from seeded scenarios; excludes navigation, retries and extra selections.
findings.recommendation: After a learner demonstrates a day manually, consider a copy-day action that still exposes and validates changed constraints. Validate with observed real learners before adding automation.

findings.observation: The current Scheduling finish checks an executable two-week model, but does not require a learner to explain a tradeoff, communicate a handover, defend the plan, or solve an infeasible demand case. Analysis level12 checks report scope and pooled rate, not the entire statistical path.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified scope of automated checks; effectiveness cannot be inferred
findings.reproduction: Inspected final-level generators, checkers, finish and saved-state fields. No required rationale, peer review, or communication work product is present in the game paths.
findings.recommendation: Use the game as fundamentals practice. Add a later unfamiliar combined mission with a small decision artifact and human review before treating stars as job-proficiency evidence.

findings.observation: A single Hint lowers the maximum score for the current case to one star, while any number of failed checks can still earn two. This makes a deliberate request for instruction look worse than repeated unassisted guessing.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: scoring rule verified; learner avoidance is a hypothesis
findings.reproduction: Read finish() precedence and showHelp(); hints are recorded before the dialog opens.
findings.recommendation: Consider separating practice help from a later independent challenge, or showing coached/independent badges without presenting help-seeking as poorer learning.

findings.observation: Baseline Check, Plan flights and Set wave controls lacked stable focus identifiers although render() replaced the entire UI. Keyboard focus could be lost after checking or changing a board wave. A large board also places many cells in the normal tab sequence.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: missing focus identifiers verified from source; root handles browser confirmation
findings.reproduction: Compare action controls against render() focus-restoration logic. Pack tiles and aircraft cells already had data-focus; primary check controls did not.
findings.recommendation: Root is adding stable focus restoration. Separately consider arrow-key grid navigation for the checkerboard.
findings.status: Fixed for primary check/action controls. Browser verification passed. Arrow-key grid navigation remains a recommendation.

findings.observation: Mean uses exactly four integer-balance stacks; median uses five distinct values; scatter/report claims use a small fixed option set. These make a clear introduction but do not yet exercise even-sized medians, fractional means, sample-size uncertainty or a learner-authored explanation.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified content scope; transfer difficulty is a hypothesis
findings.reproduction: Inspected scenario families and final checks. No even-sized median or inferential statistics case is generated in the new game path.
findings.recommendation: Extend later levels only after validating these foundations; keep the initial game uncluttered.

findings.observation: All four worlds reuse the same underlying models with different vocabulary, vehicles and progress tracks. Different-world success alone would not establish transfer to independent industry constraints.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified implementation scope; transfer measurement is a design inference
findings.reproduction: The same Flight engine and Analysis pack are used for every world; world values are passed to rendering.
findings.recommendation: Retain playful worlds. Later use genuinely different constraint sets and unseen tasks when testing transfer, rather than counting a skin change as a new occupational test.

findings.observation: Stars and current work are browser-local. The main game does not provide a trainer report/export of decisions, mistakes or work products, unlike the separate earlier practice workspace.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified main-game feature scope
findings.reproduction: Inspected persistence shape and menu actions; localStorage contains current state and best stars but no trainer-facing export action.
findings.recommendation: A working-group pilot needs a lightweight results sheet or separate observation form; add an optional work-product export later without interrupting play.

personas.value: A newcomer can begin by selecting aircraft without reading a maintenance manual.
personas.concern: The first request for a hint earns fewer stars than repeated failed checks, which may discourage asking how the game works.

personas.value: The Bus Company setting makes the relationship between vehicles and repeated trips approachable.
personas.concern: Later boards could feel like a large amount of scrolling and repeated tapping on a phone; confirm this with actual phone users.

personas.value: Named buttons and aircraft labels support keyboard access to the opening exercises.
personas.concern: Primary actions could lose keyboard focus after rerendering in the baseline build.

personas.value: The level map lets a curious newcomer see the destination before committing to a sequence.
personas.concern: Skipping directly to a checkerboard may bypass the cues that explain curing and work placement.

personas.value: The shared-cure exercise makes a scheduling efficiency visible as fewer grounded days.
personas.concern: A learner should be able to explain why the shared cure is valid in this fictional model before transferring the shortcut to real work.

personas.value: Small daily missions give a practical foothold before the whole checkerboard appears.
personas.concern: The jump from9 core actions in level6 to48 in level7 may add input effort faster than it adds new concepts.

personas.value: Undo and source-specific error messages make incorrect assignments recoverable.
personas.concern: A later112-cell board remains cumbersome to traverse one Tab at a time even after focus is repaired.

personas.value: The final outage provides a reason to revise an existing plan rather than rebuild mindlessly.
personas.concern: New cases retain the same structural pattern, so a changed tail number is a limited test of adaptation.

personas.value: Feasible alternatives are accepted; the game does not demand the authors one exact schedule.
personas.concern: The model lacks dock capacity, labor qualifications and other resource constraints needed for a later job-level assessment.

personas.value: A compact checkerboard can make availability and commitments visible together.
personas.concern: The135 core actions in level12 may reward patience with tapping as well as planning skill.

personas.value: Cell labels identify aircraft, day and wave status rather than relying on color alone.
personas.concern: A keyboard scheduler needs predictable continuation at the next relevant work cell after each command.

personas.value: Direct level access respects an experienced scheduler who already understands six-turn-four.
personas.concern: Every generated capstone is solvable; there is no decision about escalating impossible demand or accepting a tradeoff.

personas.value: The progression isolates useful teaching points, especially active work versus elapsed curing.
personas.concern: The trainer cannot yet ask the game to distinguish guided practice from a separate unseen independent assessment.

personas.value: Students can enter the game on a browser without a large document download.
personas.concern: Students on multiple devices will not automatically bring their progress or artifacts to a shared trainer view.

personas.value: Worked examples are marked as demonstrations and do not earn independent stars.
personas.concern: Zero demo stars are useful, but completion alone does not show whether the learner could reproduce the reasoning.

personas.value: A trainer can move directly to a selected challenge during a discussion.
personas.concern: The working group needs an easy way to inspect the finished work and the reason for choices, beyond the star total.

personas.value: The final model checks both maintenance work and flying commitments.
personas.concern: A two-week eight-asset solution does not yet demonstrate the users larger occupational capstone.

personas.value: Airline and Bus Company make the underlying resource-allocation problem recognizable outside military vocabulary.
personas.concern: A whimsical world may engage some staff and distract others; preference needs real-user observation, not an invented approval percentage.

personas.value: Explicitly bounded game rules help separate fictional practice from actual maintenance instructions.
personas.concern: A supervisor should interpret stars as game feedback, not as evidence of independent job qualification.

personas.value: The changed-demand level is a useful starting point for a scenario-based working-group discussion.
personas.concern: The app still needs a final communicate-and-defend activity to match the full performance framework.

personas.value: Selecting completed jobs introduces the distinction between planned and finished work through an action.
personas.concern: The completed-job target count is visible, so this proves classification more directly than independent counting.

personas.value: The first analysis cases are short enough to enter without facing a spreadsheet full of numbers.
personas.concern: A newcomer may avoid Hint because of the scoring penalty even when the instruction is unfamiliar.

personas.value: Number tiles and source records are ordinary buttons with labels.
personas.concern: The baseline primary Check action needed stable focus after feedback.

personas.value: A newcomer can try a chart challenge directly and return to counting when ready.
personas.concern: Jumping to pooled reports without learning denominator scope may create guessing rather than a useful challenge.

personas.value: Assembling the numerator and denominator makes the rate structure visible.
personas.concern: Both pooled/report denominators were always100 in the baseline. This memorization shortcut is now corrected for new cases.

personas.value: Moving tokens to balance four stacks gives a concrete image of the mean.
personas.concern: Only whole-number means from four stacks are practiced, so fractional averages need a later bridge.

personas.value: The missing-value case requires the matching day and unit, not only the right number.
personas.concern: A correct filled value must remain tied to its evidence after later edits; the reducer tests verify this behavior.

personas.value: The first report requires selecting the correct time window instead of including every visible row.
personas.concern: Fixed answer sets can demonstrate recognition without requiring the learner to construct an explanation.

personas.value: Pooling actual counts teaches why group size matters.
personas.concern: Unequal groups need varied totals; baseline totals of100 did not adequately vary the denominator. New cases now do.

personas.value: Comparing equal means with different spreads introduces a useful operational distinction.
personas.concern: The spread lesson uses range alone; a later extension should distinguish range, distribution and sample size.

personas.value: Charts include text descriptions and visible observation values.
personas.concern: Level was an impossible correct answer in baseline trend/scatter replay. Neutral cases are now included.

personas.value: The game rewards a scoped statement rather than a claim guaranteed forever.
personas.concern: The final report does not yet combine trends, variation or unfamiliar evidence into the same decision.

personas.value: The stages separate counting, rates, center, missing data, trends and reporting.
personas.concern: The introductory sequence is promising, but a trainer still needs an unseen transfer task before claiming learning.

personas.value: The simple game can be an approachable first exposure before a larger statistics lab.
personas.concern: Repeated fixed-layout scenarios may teach where to click; vary the problem structure after the basics.

personas.value: Reducers preserve prior states, and Undo supports discussing a mistaken analytical step.
personas.concern: Keyboard focus and concise error feedback matter when a trainer demonstrates a wrong denominator live.

personas.value: A trainer can select the exact concept that a learner is having trouble applying.
personas.concern: The neutral scatter correction must say no clear linear trend rather than claiming that no relationship exists; the patch does.

personas.value: A correct rate requires the right records and matching counts, not merely a plausible percentage.
personas.concern: Completion stars do not show that a learner can investigate a bad source, make a decision and defend it independently.

personas.value: World vocabulary connects the same analytic structure to flights, runs, visits or missions.
personas.concern: Changing the world alone does not add a distinct industry data model or demonstrate occupational transfer.

personas.value: The code explicitly rejects causal conclusions drawn only from the shown scatter.
personas.concern: No causal choice is valid in these observational scenarios, appropriately; later learning should still demand reasoning beyond remembering that rule.

personas.value: The last challenge assembles a small report from competing records and a time window.
personas.concern: A supervisor needs inspectable evidence of the actual report and rationale, not only a best score.

component_reviews.title: Simulated MXMGR review — Documentation and Data Integrity
component_reviews.method: 40 constructed perspectives, not human participants. Every persona is an evaluation lens. Code and deterministic event-path tests cover all ten levels in each specialty across 20 seeds; these tests are not modeled human success rates. Source/render probes verified two concrete baseline defects. Persona reactions and transfer concerns remain hypotheses for real users.

findings.observation: Baseline Documentation level 10 reused the same answer focus keys across auto-advanced tabs. After choosing the correct first asset, focus could land on the correct answer in every following tab, allowing repeated Enter to supply the remaining answers.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified source/model defect; browser reproduction is owned by root.
findings.reproduction: For seeds 1–20, every tab contained data-focus="doc-pack-a" and id a was the correct choice; repeating that focus identity solved all five links. Baseline probe: records-probes.cjs.
findings.recommendation: Give options slot-specific focus keys and move focus to the next tab control after choosing an answer.
findings.status: Fixed in pack and shared shell. Browser verified focus moves to the next stage tab, not its correct answer.

findings.observation: Baseline Integrity level 10 recorded review of an already-correct row internally but rendered an identical board before and after; the player had no persistent per-row sign that review was complete.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified source/render defect.
findings.reproduction: Copy/verify row d in level10 for seeds1–20. reviewed gains d but the complete rendered board HTML was identical.
findings.recommendation: Persist a Reviewed label/checkmark and accessible pressed state for reviewed rows.
findings.status: Fixed. Browser verified visible/accessibility Reviewed state; model probes cover already-correct rows.

findings.observation: Integrity levels 1,2,8 and10 correct every field via one Match source action. The final batch still supplies the authoritative source beside each record and one-click correction; it does not require selecting which fields or source facts support a correction.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified interaction scope; possible effect on independent proficiency is a hypothesis.
findings.reproduction: The copy reducer replaces the whole record with sources[eventId], including identity,value and units.
findings.recommendation: Keep this as initial scaffolding; add a later challenge with plausible source candidates, field-level corrections and a choice of keep, correct, hold, or investigate.
findings.status: Backlog; not changed during focused fixes.

findings.observation: The Documentation final pack is five cued choices. Its source card tells the required asset, approved revision, kit and acceptable timing; it does not make the player discover requirements from an unfamiliar work product or defend a decision.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified curriculum scope; transfer concern is a hypothesis.
findings.reproduction: Follow the five labeled tabs; each shows three candidates and explicit target details.
findings.recommendation: Follow the game foundation with a short unfamiliar case that combines applicability, due forecasting, register reconciliation and closeout evidence without identifying every target first.

findings.observation: Documentation forecasting uses exact constant daily usage and integer days. It teaches the earlier-of-two-limits rule, but not changed demand, fractional threshold crossing or forecasting uncertainty.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified model simplification; difficulty or real-world transfer effect needs users.
findings.reproduction: Level5 sets limit=now+daily*usageDays and compares that exact day with a calendar day.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the simple first exercise and add a later changed-use-rate case or one that asks whether more evidence is needed.

findings.observation: Documentation register repair stores trail strings such as Linked R-123 or Archived R-OLD; replacing a row does not retain its old interval or old row contents in that trail. Integrity later teaches a fuller before-and-after trail.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified difference in modeled traceability; instructional inconsistency risk is a hypothesis.
findings.reproduction: Replace the incorrect interval in Documentation9; p.trail records the linked requirement ID but not the previous interval.
findings.recommendation: In an advanced register exercise, retain before/after/source/reason for replacements and archive actions, consistent with Integrity.

findings.observation: A hint limits a case to one star, while failed checks followed by correction can still earn two. The game therefore rewards unsupported trial-and-error more highly than intentionally asking for help.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified scoring rule; whether it discourages help is a simulated-user hypothesis.
findings.reproduction: finish chooses assisted?0:hints?1:mistakes?2:3.
findings.recommendation: Keep assisted and independent attempts distinguishable, but consider separate practice rewards and independent-check badges so learners are not discouraged from opening a hint.
findings.status: Backlog; no change to established scoring during this review.

findings.observation: Worlds change context labels, icons, vehicles and seed/progress state; the core Documentation and Integrity task structures stay the same.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified architecture; user preferences and transfer to civilian occupations remain hypotheses.
findings.reproduction: Render any case with each world object; requirements and validators remain the same.
findings.recommendation: Describe these as contextual worlds around shared fundamentals. Later add genuinely different constraints when industry-specific transfer is the goal.

findings.observation: The game shell primarily preserves current work and best stars. It does not present an assessor with a comparable portfolio showing reasoning, unseen-case performance and an explanation rubric across the two record specialties.
source: README.md: game scope versus preserved courses workspace
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified current game scope; sufficiency for job qualification must be evaluated separately.
findings.reproduction: Game completion shows stars and a short reveal, then next-level/new-case/review choices.
findings.recommendation: Keep stars as game feedback. Add an optional later independent work-product challenge and assessor rubric if the working group wants evidence of practical proficiency.
findings.status: Backlog; not a claim of measured training effectiveness.

findings.observation: Several compact-screen metadata labels are rendered at 9–10px; record comparison and register tasks rely on these details.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: CSS sizes verified; readability concern is a hypothesis requiring real device/user testing.
findings.reproduction: Inspect sg-card-meta, sg-label and sg-note in the small-screen rules.
findings.recommendation: Check on a physical phone with typical users; prioritize asset IDs, intervals, units and source status over decorative labels, and support enlarged text.

findings.observation: Documentation validators correctly enforce both applicability conditions, current approved instructions, prerequisite order, matching evidence and the absence of duplicate/extra requirements. Alternative register row order and either parts/slot prerequisite order are accepted.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified by source and passing model/event tests.
findings.reproduction: Run tests/pack-documentation.cjs; checks include extra tagged assets, draft revisions, reordered valid prerequisites, duplicate requirements and alternative register order.
findings.recommendation: Retain these checks and acceptance of valid alternatives.

findings.observation: Current-source exercises show one approved source, one superseded source and one draft. They do not yet include two approved versions with different effective dates or conflicting authoritative records.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified scenario pattern; risk of learning only the Approved label is a hypothesis.
findings.reproduction: Generate any seed; source status categories and correct status remain fixed.
findings.recommendation: Add a later source-selection case with more than one approved-looking record, an effective-date boundary or an unresolved conflict requiring investigation.

findings.observation: Applicability and period-selection meters reveal the number of required selections, which is helpful scaffolding but reduces the need to decide whether the search is complete.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified UI behavior; influence on learning is a hypothesis.
findings.reproduction: Untouched tasks show tagged/records selected against the exact number expected.
findings.recommendation: Keep counts in introductory play; remove the answer-count cue in a later independent challenge while retaining an explicit Check action.

findings.observation: Documentation will not close a job with only a plan, a wrong-asset record or a failed check; editing linked evidence reopens the closeout.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified by model tests.
findings.reproduction: Attempt stamp with incomplete evidence, or remove an evidence link after a valid closeout.
findings.recommendation: Retain the distinction between scheduled and verified-completed work.

findings.observation: Integrity preserves unknown-versus-zero, requires matching units, distinguishes a duplicate event from a similar event, retains zero-result records in period totals, rejects overbroad zero filtering and checks correction history.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: Verified by source and model/event tests.
findings.reproduction: Run tests/pack-integrity.cjs; the negative cases cover each distinction and both valid duplicate-removal alternatives.
findings.recommendation: Retain these fundamentals and make them recur in later mixed challenges.

personas.value: The first record match gives an immediate, concrete starting point.
personas.concern: A newcomer may mistake the act of attaching a requirement for evidence that the inspection itself is complete.

personas.value: Short prompts and large asset cards offer a manageable first phone task.
personas.concern: Small applicability and interval metadata may require zooming on a physical phone.

personas.value: Buttons and explicit labels can support keyboard-only play.
personas.concern: The baseline capstone reused answer-focus identities and could silently focus the next correct answer.

personas.value: Open level selection lets an impatient learner explore the later work pack.
personas.concern: Skipping to the final pack can produce a completion badge without practicing applicability or forecast decisions.

personas.value: Combining family and serial range is more useful than memorizing a definition.
personas.concern: Exact target counts may let a learner stop searching when the meter fills rather than verifying applicability.

personas.value: The first-due-day challenge clearly introduces two competing limits.
personas.concern: The fixed-use forecast may look easier than a changing operational forecast, and compact source cards need a real-phone check.

personas.value: The register supports alternative valid row ordering.
personas.concern: A replacement records only a short Linked message, so the old interval is not visible in the register trail.

personas.value: New cases change asset numbers and intervals.
personas.concern: The final five-choice structure remains predictable even when numbers change.

personas.value: Current, draft and superseded copies teach a useful source-control distinction.
personas.concern: A veteran may find a single Approved choice too obvious to exercise judgment.

personas.value: The matching-work-plus-passed-check closeout is a practical distinction.
personas.concern: The strongest evidence labels become small on phone layouts; real users should confirm they can compare them easily.

personas.value: Either parts-first or slot-first is accepted when prerequisites are satisfied.
personas.concern: The baseline auto-advance focus rewarded repeated activation instead of deliberate inspection of the next stage.

personas.value: The work-pack path brings several basic decisions together quickly.
personas.concern: It still cues each target and has no conflicting sources, changed demand or reasoned defense.

personas.value: A trainer can demonstrate wrong applicability, wrong revisions and invalid closeouts safely.
personas.concern: Stars alone do not show which concept the learner misunderstood or whether the learner can repeat the task independently.

personas.value: A trainer can use the phone-friendly cards during short practice sessions.
personas.concern: Hint scoring could discourage a learner from requesting the help the trainer wants them to use.

personas.value: Keyboard play can make a projector walkthrough efficient.
personas.concern: Automatic focus must move to the next stage, not a preselected correct answer; the pack fix now supplies that target.

personas.value: Direct access to any level helps a trainer target a weak skill.
