personas.concern: A later unseen work-product challenge is needed if the trainer wants evidence beyond recognition of the displayed cues.

personas.value: The model accepts valid alternatives and enforces prerequisite logic.
personas.concern: A supervisor should not read a best-star total as demonstrated job qualification.

personas.value: Short sessions can fit around work without a long lesson page.
personas.concern: The supervisor still needs observable work products and a practical review rubric to compare learners.

personas.value: The correct-current-source rule and reopened closeout reinforce documentation discipline.
personas.concern: The simpler register history should eventually preserve before/after detail so both record specialties teach compatible audit habits.

personas.value: World changes show that the underlying record skills are broader than one aircraft community.
personas.concern: Changing the label to a bus or rover does not by itself establish transfer to a different occupation.

personas.value: One wrong number gives a novice an easy first success.
personas.concern: The Match source button performs the correction automatically; a novice can succeed without identifying the mismatched field.

personas.value: Unknown and zero appear side by side with short labels.
personas.concern: Their small metadata should remain readable on a real phone so the distinction is not reduced to blind tapping.

personas.value: Source and record cards make the evidence relationship visible.
personas.concern: An already-correct retained row originally had no persistent reviewed marker after keyboard verification.

personas.value: Immediate corrections make experimentation feel safe.
personas.concern: An impatient player may press Match source on every row and learn the button sequence more readily than the verification habit.

personas.value: Unit conversion requires choosing both a number and a unit.
personas.concern: A later mixed-unit batch would be needed to see whether this carries over when the unit mismatch is not announced in the prompt.

personas.value: Event IDs and times make duplicate comparison concrete.
personas.concern: Side-by-side comparisons and small labels may become tiring on a phone during a larger batch.

personas.value: Linking child records to existing parents gives a concrete identity task.
personas.concern: The reviewed-state marker was necessary so keyboard users could keep their place in a mixed batch.

personas.value: Keeping zero-result records teaches a useful reconciliation habit.
personas.concern: The exact expected record count is displayed, so the task does not yet assess when the search is complete.

personas.value: Duplicate events are distinguished from similar but separate events.
personas.concern: An experienced reviewer will want ambiguous duplicates and investigation choices, beyond identical event copies.

personas.value: The current-source challenge correctly rejects a newer draft.
personas.concern: There is always exactly one Approved choice; real source disputes require more than noticing that label.

personas.value: The before-and-after audit trail is a useful foundation.
personas.concern: Baseline review of an unchanged record was invisible, making a correct batch harder to inspect; that display issue is now fixed.

personas.value: The prevention gate holds errors while retaining valid zeros.
personas.concern: The final batch still supplies the authoritative answer beside every row and copies whole records in one action.

personas.value: A trainer can demonstrate why an unknown cannot be changed to zero.
personas.concern: The trainer needs a later task that requires the learner to choose a correction, not merely request an automatic copy.

personas.value: Short tasks can support frequent practice and immediate discussion.
personas.concern: The star cost of hints may undermine the trainer’s invitation to ask for help.

personas.value: Persistent Reviewed indicators now make it easier to explain which rows have been checked.
personas.concern: Keyboard and screen-reader behavior still needs live-user validation rather than relying solely on render tests.

personas.value: A trainer can jump to the exact misconception: units, duplicates, period or source.
personas.concern: Completing a targeted example does not show independent transfer to an unfamiliar combined case.

personas.value: The gate checks model prevention as well as cleanup.
personas.concern: A supervisor would need evidence that learners can distinguish hold/investigate from correct when sources conflict.

personas.value: Local browser play makes a small exercise easy to start.
personas.concern: Current stars do not offer a comparable assessor portfolio or explanation of judgment.

personas.value: Audit validation checks more than whether the final number happens to be right.
personas.concern: Record review and correction history should become part of a larger work-product assessment, not be inferred from stars.

personas.value: Airline, bus, cat and squirrel contexts make the same record relationships approachable.
personas.concern: The contexts share the same underlying task patterns; they are not evidence of four independent occupational validations.

changes.change: Unique answer focus keys per tab; result.focus points to the newly active tab control; regressions cover target existence and removal of previous answer identity.
Reviewed checkmark, label and aria-pressed state persist after row verification, including unchanged correct records; render regressions added.

component_reviews.title: Database Management and assessment review —20 simulated MXMGR perspectives

methodology.participants: No real participants. Twenty constructed role/context perspectives, not twenty independent empirical observations.
methodology.coverage: All10 Database Management levels reviewed through source and pure-model/shell probes; cross-specialty assessment concerns refer to the shared main game shell.
methodology.matrix: Five experience profiles × four play contexts/worlds. Worlds are assigned review contexts, not evidence that twenty human players used them.
actual_methods: DOM-free execution of real shell event handlers
Published-generator comparison for legacy case compatibility

findings.observation: The ten-level path introduces access keys, scope, expiry, offboarding, unique identity, dependencies, controlled change, recovery, then a combined service challenge. Seeded action tests find each level solvable and reject several important invalid states.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified software behavior; learning benefit remains a hypothesis
findings.reproduction: Run node tests/pack-database.cjs. Original suite passed2053 assertions; after focused fixes the suite passed4301.
findings.recommendation: Keep the one-action opening and progressively combined work. Do not add a prerequisite lecture.

findings.observation: Before this review, completing a shown example wrote best[level]=0 yet displayed the same completed checkmark and incremented the same specialty completion count as independent work. This did not award stars, but the completion display blurred the distinction.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified in real shell event harness
findings.reproduction: Database level1 → Show a working example → Open access → Next level. Persisted best={1:0}; level1 got class="level-dot done" and check icon; Object.keys(best).length=1.
findings.recommendation: Implemented by root: demonstrations remain recorded but have a distinct demo marker and do not contribute to completed-level counts.
findings.status: fixed by root in shared shell; root reports225 shell assertions passing

findings.observation: The published DBM10 generator changed names and button order but repeated the same two access requests, same excess/missing key positions and same broken connection. One hundred seeds produced one substantive constraint pattern.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified generator limitation; fixed in local source
findings.reproduction: Normalize names and key-bank order; compare actors task/scope/required keys, initial grants and broken dependency across seeds1–100. Before:1 pattern. After:51 patterns, with36 connection,34 database and30 report failures.
findings.recommendation: Implemented varied scope/task pairs, actor access correction positions and failed dependencies. Existing saved DBM10 work keeps revision1; new cases use revision2.
findings.status: fixed; revision1 exactly matches published generator for100seeds

findings.observation: The unique-identity exercise originally labeled the target account Approved and the other No request, so a player could find the answer without matching the unique identifier on the source request.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified source/render shortcut; fixed in local source
findings.reproduction: Inspect both account task chips in level6. Published labels disclosed the requested account. New labels both say View reports; approval and unique ID remain on the separate source request.
findings.recommendation: Implemented neutral account task labels. Preserve the duplicate display name and require the identifier to distinguish accounts.

findings.observation: Recovery verifies only an expected record count after restore/replay. The model has no record contents, reconciliation samples, duplicates or last-transaction evidence to inspect.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified model scope; risk of transfer overconfidence is a hypothesis
findings.reproduction: Level9 state contains restored,replayed,verified,opened,count. Verify succeeds when count equals snapshot+pending and stage flags are true.
findings.recommendation: Keep count verification as the introductory task. Add a later recovery case that compares sample contents or transaction evidence, ideally crossing into Data Integrity.

findings.observation: Troubleshooting displays the single failed component directly and repairs it with one action. This practices recognizing a dependency and leaving healthy components alone, but does not require diagnosis from incomplete symptoms.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified model scope; experienced-user reaction is simulated
findings.reproduction: Every case has one false node, explicitly labeled with its failure and Tap to repair; healthy-node clicks leave state unchanged.
findings.recommendation: Retain the simple opening. Later introduce an inspect step, downstream symptoms, and a choice of corrective action rather than only clicking the displayed failure.

findings.observation: Main-game stars measure no failed checks, corrected work, hint use and example use. The shell does not collect a rationale, briefing, independent assessor rating, time-to-proficiency record or cross-specialty work product. It therefore does not establish the full Discover→Evaluate→Decide→Act→Communicate→Defend objective.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified main-game evidence scope; proposed evaluation design is a recommendation
findings.reproduction: Inspect persisted current state and best stars, then finish a game level. No communication/defense artifact or assessor rubric is produced by the game path. Earlier practice workspace is separate.
findings.recommendation: Use the game as fundamentals practice. Follow with an unfamiliar combined work task, a brief explanation of choices and independent assessor review; compare with baseline and delayed transfer before claiming four-hour proficiency or tenfold efficiency.

findings.observation: Using a hint reduces the same-case result to one star. A learner focused on collecting stars might avoid asking for help, even during initial learning. No actual learner behavior was observed.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: scoring rule verified; behavioral effect explicitly hypothetical
findings.reproduction: Hint → solve correctly gives one star. A new case resets assistance. Restart and Undo retain it.
findings.recommendation: During a real pilot, observe help-seeking and frustration. Consider separate practice encouragement and independent-challenge badges if star pressure discourages learning.

findings.observation: The main game stores its current case and best stars locally by world and specialty, but it does not expose a portable record of learner decisions for a working-group evaluator. Earlier workspace exports do not represent the new game path.
findings.verified_or_hypothesis: verified implementation boundary; workflow impact is simulated
findings.reproduction: Inspect main game menu and progress object: world/skill/current/best exist; no learner-evidence export action or cross-device account workflow exists.
findings.recommendation: For a pilot, use a short observer sheet or later add an optional local progress/evidence export. Do not interpret browser-local stars as an authenticated qualification record.

personas.value: One request and three keys make the first action easy to understand.
personas.concern: I may assume Edit alone is enough until I notice that viewing and editing are separate capabilities in this game.

personas.value: A short instruction and a few buttons suit a quick practice break.
personas.concern: I need the task, person, scope and selected keys to remain visible together on a small display; this requires browser observation, not a claim from code alone.

personas.value: Labeled buttons and stable focus identifiers give a basis for keyboard interaction.
personas.concern: I want a real keyboard walkthrough to confirm that a repaired/re-rendered board does not strand focus; this review did not use a browser.

personas.value: I can jump to the task that catches my attention and return to fundamentals.
personas.concern: If I skip straight to the final service challenge, I may click failure markers without understanding the approval and change sequence.

personas.value: Permissions, room scope and temporary passes connect to everyday account work.
personas.concern: The old identity labels let me choose Approved without reading the unique ID; neutral labels now make that distinction meaningful.

personas.value: Local saved work lets me leave a short task and return to it on the same browser.
personas.concern: My progress will not automatically follow from my phone to a work computer, and an evaluator cannot infer that these are the same learner.

personas.value: Wrong ordering is rejected and I can correct a sequence instead of starting a long lesson again.
personas.concern: The detailed error tells me the right order; the resulting corrected-work stars should not be treated as an independent assessment.

personas.value: The final challenge combines access, a dependency and a safe change in one place.
personas.concern: Repeated final cases previously reused the same action pattern; varied tasks and failures now require me to read the case again.

personas.value: The early levels are a useful quick check of least-privilege and access-lifecycle habits.
personas.concern: A directly marked failed node is too simple to establish that I can diagnose an interface fault from ambiguous symptoms.

personas.value: The modular path lets me practice during short intervals without a setup procedure.
personas.concern: I would need a later recovery task that validates actual records; matching a count alone leaves important integrity questions unasked.

personas.value: The duplicate-name exercise rewards a precise identifier comparison after the label shortcut was removed.
personas.concern: The case still tests a small predetermined permission set; my broader judgement about approvals and exceptional access is not measured.

personas.value: Level selection lets me bypass already-familiar introductory key puzzles.
personas.concern: Four different worlds are context changes around the same mechanics, so completing each is not four independent occupational qualifications.

personas.value: Working examples and repeatable seeded cases support demonstration followed by guided practice.
personas.concern: A zero-star demo used to display the same completed checkmark as independent work; the distinction must survive menus and progress summaries.

personas.value: One concept per short task offers a practical way to observe a learner without a slide presentation.
personas.concern: I need to see whether the learner avoids Hint to protect stars; that effect cannot be established by this simulated panel.

personas.value: Separate world and specialty progress supports individual pacing and returning to unfinished work.
personas.concern: A trainer still needs a way to record the reason behind a learner decision and compare independent performance across unfamiliar cases.

personas.value: The now-varied final DBM case is more useful for asking a learner to inspect each new request.
personas.concern: The same visible failure cues and fixed safe-change sequence still make this practice, not a fully independent practical examination.

personas.value: The five-specialty structure makes the expected fundamentals visible and easy to discuss with a working group.
personas.concern: I cannot answer who is ready to perform the full job from game completion alone; I need an unfamiliar work product and its defense.

personas.value: A browser game lowers the effort required to demonstrate the concept to colleagues.
personas.concern: Local browser scores are not an auditable team proficiency record and may be lost when moving devices or clearing data.

personas.value: The playful setting can make the same permission and record concepts approachable outside aviation.
personas.concern: Accessibility and appeal still need observation with actual users; this role simulation is not evidence of adoption or training effectiveness.

personas.value: Open navigation makes it easy to inspect later tasks without completing every earlier screen.
personas.concern: Fast completion, including using examples, must not be used to claim the four-hour or tenfold training targets were achieved.
